title: Fifteen-year fits gave no clear six-month ENSO forecast gain over expanding fits at 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether a shorter training record improves six-month forecasts of monthly Nino 3.4 temperature anomalies. Both fits used seasonal surface terms and NOAA GODAS basin warm water volume. Fits used only eligible earlier targets. For 300 origins in 2000-2024, the 15-year fit had 9.68% higher mean squared error than an expanding fit from 1980. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -23.16% to +3.20%. Root mean squared error rose from 0.6480 C to 0.6786 C. Ten-year and twenty-year fits also had higher point errors. Removing any one scored year left the primary difference negative. These results give no clear benefit from the 15-year fit. They do not show that ENSO dynamics are constant or identify why the shorter fit had more error. Revised data, one linear model, few events and conditional intervals limit inference. The package includes original code, source provenance, aggregate errors, a figure and a separate numerical audit. External records are regenerated outside the signed package.

display.caption: Shorter and expanding fits at six-month leads. Negative MSE reduction means more error. Bars give marginal conditional 95% three-year block intervals.

citations.reason: Published model structure and frozen public sources motivate this direct training-window test. Data overlap; no independent confirmation. No code was copied.
